parameters.reference:
NOT PINNED — run_corpus_combine.sh:80 passes no --ref, and the product header records NO reference key at all (checked for REF/ANCHOR/SETREF: none). THIS FIELD HAS BEEN WRONG TWICE; read the provenance of each clause before quoting it.
MEASURED AND CURRENT — the auto-pick takes INDEX 0, the first member in link order. reference_member = s_00001 in ALL TEN compose gate records on this rig (13/17/22/25/52/77 members), and confirmed experimentally: a compose with no --ref is BIT-IDENTICAL to the same compose with --ref=1, 0 differing pixels of 98,194,977. It does NOT rank. Consequence: appending a night re-bases nothing; only a night that sorts FIRST, or a reordering of the session arguments, re-bases anything.
MEASURED AND CURRENT — --ref IS LIVE ON THE SHIPPED (seqplatesolve/astrometric) ROUTE, both halves of the doctrine. One-knob probe, 4 members, 2 nights, only --ref differing: canvas 7071x4629 -> 7095x4622; north angle +9.62 -> +7.76 deg; centre median R/G/B [39.9,157.4,116.9] -> [26.9,90.5,47.6]; B/G 0.7427 -> 0.5260. Canvas/orientation from the product WCS (astropy, naxis=2, centre pixel); medians from Siril `stat` via regional_stat.py. So the reference moves the canvas AND the raw channel balance.
WITHDRAWN — an earlier revision of this field claimed the ORIENTATION half was FALSE on the shipped route, from composites measuring -0.44/+0.32 deg while members measure -164.77/+164.35/-176.57 deg. The measurement is right and the INFERENCE was wrong: comparing composites to members is observational and cannot isolate the knob. What it actually shows is that the canvas does not INHERIT the reference's orientation; the one-knob probe shows the reference nonetheless MOVES it. The doctrine's stated mechanism ('the canvas inherits the reference's orientation', docs/dead-ends.md, measured on the star-pair route) is imprecise on this route; its CONSEQUENCE — pin the reference on a multi-night compose — holds and is now measured here.
STILL UNCHECKED: by what RULE the astrometric canvas orientation tracks the reference. Two points show it moves; they do not give the relation. A deterministic pin does not need the relation, so nothing here depends on it — do not treat it as characterised.
CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY A/B: this product is NOT a --ref control. It was built with no --ref, so bit-identity against it can only be achieved by reproducing the auto-pick — the behaviour a derivation exists to replace. A --ref derivation changes this product BY CONSTRUCTION and is a DECLARED DELTA, not a no-op. It IS a valid control for --central (0.5) and --max-stars (default 200).

solve.DEFECT_FOUND_IN_finish_render: finish_render.sh line 143 hardcodes --max-stars=400 and does not expose it. On this Milky-Way field that produced logodds 63 — FLOOR-CLASS, below the confident-match floor of 100 — where the default 200 gives 106. solve_field.py's own docstring gives the mechanism: brightest-first selection clusters stars in the galactic band, so 400 over-constrains the order-3 SIP fit and leaves the corners extrapolating. The rendered surface above was produced by running finish_render's stages MANUALLY with max-stars=200; the shipped script would still emit a floor-class solve. NOT FIXED — build-path change, owner's call.
solve.also: run_corpus_combine.sh never passes --central either, though finish_render accepts it and a framing=max union's coverage seams false-detect. Two blind attempts burned 89 minutes before --central solved it in 6 seconds.
